newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Davids says full year profit to fall.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Davids says full year profit to fall.

text.p: Food wholesaler and retailer Davids Ltd said on Tuesday that its full year profit after abnormals would be below the 1995/96 level, based on an assessment of trading results in the past four months.

The Sydney-based company, which competes in the retail market with Woolworths Ltd and Coles Myer Ltd among others, said anticipated profits had been affected by weak trading conditions in February across most business units and the continued costs of integrating QIW/CBL acquired in May 1996.

It also cited the restructuring costs of Campbells Cash and Carry, saying costs had been affected by a successful court appeal by a competitor which dealt with the company's branch network. Davids achieved 1995/96 (July/June) net earnings of A$51.8 million from A$46.3 million a year earlier.
Executive chairman John David said joint managing director John Patten had taken an extended leave of absence due to ill health. The other joint managing director is Jeff David.

The company also said its option to acquire Davids Asia from Allind Pty Ltd had been extended by 18 months to December 31, 1998. Allind is owned by the members of thE David family, which owns 41.5 percent of the listing company.
Davids Asia operates joint ventures in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, and Indonesia.
Davids Ltd said last month that Davids Asia was not yet profitable.
Davids shares were seven cents lower at A$1.26 at 11.00 a.m. (0100 GMT). The overall market was higher.
